survived.title: water_level and carpet fan_speed use a DIFFERENT precedence than every sibling field (floor default OVERRIDES the profile), so applying a built-in mop profile immediately re-labels the room "custom"
survived.mechanism: Every sibling field resolves as `room value (if key present) else profile value`. water_level does not: after line 423 sets it from the profile, lines 432-436 overwrite it — `if floor_type.startswith("carpet"): resolved_fan_speed = fan_defaults.get(...); resolved_water_level = water_defaults.get(...)` / `elif "water_level" not in room_config: resolved_water_level = water_defaults.get(floor_type, "")`. So for a room_config that omits water_level the FLOOR default wins over the profile, and on carpet the floor default wins over the profile for fan_speed too. Executed: resolve_room_profile_for_room({'profile_name':'vacuum_mop_quick','floor_type':'hardwood'})['water_level'] == 'Low' although vacuum_mop_quick declares 'Medium'; resolve_room_profile_for_room({'profile_name':'vacuum_quick','floor_type':'carpet_low_pile'})['fan_speed'] == 'Max' although vacuum_quick declares 'Standard'. That asymmetry breaks the profile round-trip. ProfileManager._match_profile_from_fields (profiles/manager.py:153-177) builds each candidate as a bare `{"profile_name": name, "floor_type": ...}` — no water_level key — so the candidate gets the FLOOR default, while the real room (written by apply_room_profile_to_config, room_profiles.py:565, which stores the PROFILE's water_level) carries the PROFILE value. I replayed the exact protect->resolve->protect->compare pipeline over all four built-ins x five floors: vacuum_mop_quick and vacuum_mop_deep match on 'tile' ONLY (where the floor default 'Medium' coincidentally equals the profile value) and fail to match on hardwood, laminate, marble, granite, concrete and carpet; vacuum_quick fails to match on carpet_low_pile (fan Standard vs carpet default Max). _finalize_room_update (manager.py:196) then does `result["profile_name"] = matched if matched else "custom"`, and it runs on BOTH apply_room_profile (manager.py:671) and every update_room_settings save (core/manager.py:1369).
survived.user_impact: The user picks the built-in "Quick" or "Deep" mop profile for a hardwood/laminate/marble room; the save stores profile_name="custom" and the chip they just clicked deselects. Same for a plain vacuum room on low-pile carpet. Renaming a room, or changing any unrelated setting, also silently drops its profile label to "custom". The comment at manager.py:138-147 explicitly CLAIMS this asymmetry was closed by resolving the candidate under the room's floor_type — it was closed for vacuum rooms only, and the comment asserts a guard that does not cover mop rooms.
survived.guards_checked: _normalize_profile_match_value (profiles/manager.py:113-135) — lowercases and folds "off", so 'Medium' vs 'Low' is a genuine mismatch, not a casing artefact. _protected_room_config (manager.py:84-111) — forces water_level "Off" only for non-mop modes, so it masks the asymmetry for vacuum profiles and leaves it exposed for mop profiles. The mop-with-no-water correction (room_profiles.py:443-448) — does not fire, because the candidate's floor default is non-empty on hardwood ('Low'). apply_room_profile_to_config (room_profiles.py:565) — writes the profile's water_level verbatim, with no floor-default reconciliation. RoomConfig.as_dict/asdict (models/models.py:237) — confirms real rooms always carry the water_level key, so only the CANDIDATE side takes the floor-default branch, which is what creates the asymmetry.

survived.title: path_type resolves to the literal string "None" for any room backfilled by the startup migration, and that string reaches the Eufy wire payload
survived.mechanism: `resolved_path_type = str(room_config.get("path_type", resolved_profile.get("path_type", "wide")))`. The precedence is key-presence, but path_type is the one setting field whose RoomConfig default is None rather than a string (models/models.py:213, `path_type: Optional[str] = None`), and core/manager.py:424 stamps `_room.setdefault("path_type", None)` into every stored room at manager construction as an "add fields added after initial release" backfill. Present-with-None means the profile fallback is skipped and `str(None)` yields the four-character string 'None'. Executed: resolve_room_profile_for_room(room_config={...,'path_type':None})['path_type'] == 'None'. Nothing downstream sanitizes it: apply_capability_gate line 497 `path_type = str(settings.get("path_type", "wide"))` (key present, default unused), queue/queue_engine.py:285 `path_type = str(gated["path_type"])`, then line 309-310 `if supports_path: _write_room_field(..., "path_type", path_type)` with Eufy's identity rename map (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:581, `{"field_name": "path_type", "value_map": None}` — _write_room_field:180-185 passes the value through untouched). supports_path_control is True for the x10/x8 families (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:226). The value is also self-perpetuating: build_managed_rooms._default (rooms/room_manager.py:87-89) and rebuild_map_bucket._prev_or_brand (maps/map_manager.py:173-175) both return the existing value when `key in existing`, and None IS present, so the brand default 'wide' never gets a chance to replace it on any re-save.
survived.user_impact: An Eufy X10/X8 room-clean payload carries path_type:"None" instead of "wide"/"narrow" — an out-of-vocabulary enum the device did not ask for, on every run of any room that predates the path_type field. planning/run_plan.py:370 (`str(room.get("path_type","")).strip() or None`) also reads the raw room dict and produces the string 'None', so the run plan displays a path type of "None".
survived.guards_checked: apply_capability_gate line 524 `if not supports_path: path_type = "wide"` — only rescues brands WITHOUT path control (Roborock), which never puts path_type on the wire anyway; the Eufy X10/X8 that does support it is exactly the case left unguarded. _write_room_field (queue_engine.py:155-185) — no validation, no options check (unlike the per_room_live_settings options_key filter in jobs/active_job.py:1385-1393, which would have caught it). resolve_new_room_defaults (rooms/room_defaults.py:81-83) — supplies path_type for both brands' default profiles, so only pre-existing/backfilled rooms are affected. apply_room_profile_to_config line 569 — writes a real string, so a room repaired by applying a profile stops being affected.

survived.title: get_available_profile_names hardcodes the four Eufy built-in keys, so get_available_profiles silently drops every user-saved custom profile and would return {} for a brand with different catalog keys
survived.mechanism: get_available_profile_names takes only `capabilities` — no `catalog`, no `stored_profiles` — and returns one of two literal lists of the framework's own built-in keys (lines 306-317). get_available_profiles then merges builtins + stored profiles (lines 327-331) and immediately filters with `if name in allowed_names` (line 338). A user-saved profile is keyed `user_<timestamp>` (_generate_room_profile_id, profiles/manager.py:73) or `user_1` (manager.py:305), none of which is in the literal list, so every custom profile the merge just added is discarded. The `stored_profiles=` argument is accepted and then made inert. Structurally the same hole applies to a brand: the catalog reaches merge_profile_dicts but never the allow-list, so a future adapter declaring `builtins` under its own key names resolves to an empty dict.
survived.user_impact: sensor/profile.py:63-70 passes the user's stored profiles in and publishes `profile_count` / `profiles` / `profile_labels` from the result, so the "available room profiles" sensor always reports 2 or 4 and never lists a profile the user created — an automation reading that attribute cannot see custom profiles at all. No error is raised; the count simply looks plausible.
survived.guards_checked: merge_profile_dicts (line 217-233) — correctly merges stored over built-ins; the loss happens after it. sensor/profile.py:40-70 — no compensating merge, it renders the filtered dict verbatim. profiles/manager.py get_room_profiles (line 220-232) — the websocket/card path uses merge_profile_dicts directly and is NOT filtered, which is why the card still shows custom profiles and the defect is confined to the sensor. capabilities gating itself (supports_mop_features / supports_water_control) is correct for the built-ins.

The `d.get(..., "Quick")` third-level literal defeats the omission. Verified: get_room_profile(profile_name='vacuum_quick', catalog=<roborock>) returns clean_intensity 'Quick'. Because every built-in is run through normalize_room_profile (get_room_profile line 291, merge_profile_dicts line 231), the injected value is not confined to display: apply_room_profile_to_config line 566 does `updated["clean_intensity"] = normalized["clean_intensity"]`, and ProfileManager.apply_room_profile (profiles/manager.py:671-678) writes that dict back to the room store. Once written, the room's own key wins in resolve_room_profile_for_room (line 416-418) forever. It also makes the resolver's new `resolved_profile.get("clean_intensity", "")` last-resort dead — a normalized profile always has the key.

survived.title: resolve_profile_catalog's `or` fallbacks mean a brand cannot declare an intentionally EMPTY block — it silently inherits Eufy's
survived.mechanism: Every key is resolved as `block.get(k) or <EUFY CONSTANT>` (lines 166-172). `{}` and `""` are falsy, so an adapter that declares `"floor_type_water_defaults": {}` (a brand with no water axis at all), `"legacy_aliases": {}` (a brand asserting it has none), or `"builtins": {}` gets the Eufy table instead of its declared emptiness. There is no way to express "I answered, and my answer is nothing" — only absence and non-empty are distinguishable. For floor_type_water_defaults this is not cosmetic: lines 434/436/448 write whatever that table yields into the effective water_level, so a vacuum-only brand declaring `{}` would have Eufy's "Low"/"Medium" written into its rooms. Related bare-deref in the same seam: get_room_profile line 289 does `profile = merged[DEFAULT_ROOM_PROFILE_NAME]` unguarded, so a brand whose builtins omit "vacuum_quick" AND whose declared default_profile key is missing from its own builtins raises KeyError inside dispatch rather than degrading.
survived.user_impact: No shipped brand hits this today (both declare non-empty blocks), but it is a structural seam a third brand categorically cannot express — the framework's own extension point silently substitutes Eufy vocabulary for a deliberate declaration, which is the exact class of defect the adapter seam exists to prevent.

survived.title: normalize_room_profile's third-level literals are the one fallback a brand CANNOT override — the more deliberately a brand omits an axis, the more certainly it gets the Eufy literal for it
survived.mechanism: Full enumeration of literals `normalize_room_profile` can inject (lines 204-214), each as the THIRD arm of `source.get(k, d.get(k, LITERAL))` where `d` is the brand's `normalize_defaults`: label→"User Profile 1"; clean_mode→"vacuum"; fan_speed→"Max" (Eufy); water_level→"Off" (Eufy); clean_intensity→"Quick" (Eufy); path_type→"wide"; clean_passes→1; edge_mopping→False; mop_required→False. Of these, "wide"/1/False are framework-canonical (both shipped catalogs use them) and "vacuum" is the canonical mode; "Max", "Off" and "Quick" are Eufy DISPLAY vocabulary. Tracing each against the shipped Roborock catalog: `CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:153-162) declares 8 of the 9 keys, so "Max" and "Off" are shadowed — but it deliberately omits `clean_intensity` (documented at vocabulary.py:107-109: "An omitted key means the room stores nothing for it, rather than an inert 'Quick' nobody can act on"). Because the brand's own `normalize_defaults` is silent on the key, the literal `"Quick"` is what `d.get("clean_intensity", "Quick")` returns. The catalog is the mechanism a brand has for saying "I do not have this axis", and the only way it can say it is by omission — which is precisely the input that routes to the hardcoded Eufy literal. Consequence chain: `get_room_profile(profile_name=..., catalog=RB)` (line 291) returns EVERY Roborock built-in carrying `clean_intensity="Quick"`; `resolve_room_profile_for_room` line 417 then reads `resolved_profile.get("clean_intensity", "")` — the `""` last-resort fallback whose comment (lines 411-414) claims it "fires only when the room AND the brand's profile both omit the key" is DEAD for this field, because the profile side has been normalized and always carries the key.

survived.title: clean_intensity has no capability flag and reaches the Eufy wire on devices whose capability detection just concluded the intensity axis is absent
survived.mechanism: `apply_capability_gate` reads five flags (lines 487-491) and clamps five fields: clean_mode/water_level (supports_mop_features, supports_water_control), edge_mopping (supports_edge_mopping), path_type (supports_path_control), clean_passes (supports_passes). `clean_intensity` is read at line 496 — `normalize_clean_intensity(settings.get("clean_intensity", "Quick"))` — and re-emitted at line 534 with no gate whatsoever; the gate will even MANUFACTURE "Quick" for a settings dict that omits the key. Downstream, queue/queue_engine.py:301 writes it unconditionally: `_write_room_field(payload_room, room_fields, "clean_intensity", clean_intensity)`, and the Eufy adapter declares an identity mapping for it (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:578, `"clean_intensity": {"field_name": "clean_intensity", "value_map": None}`), so it lands in every per-room dict of the `room_clean` payload. Compare the three sibling fields in the same writer: water_level (line 303), edge_mopping (306) and path_type (309) are each wrapped in an `if supports_*` guard; clean_intensity is not, because no such flag exists. The sharpest evidence that this is an omission rather than a decision: core/capabilities.py:255 computes `_cleaning_intensity_present = _any_present("cleaning_intensity")` and line 295 feeds it into `supports_path_control = bool(_hints.get("supports_path_control")) or _cleaning_intensity_present` — the detector probes for the CLEANING-INTENSITY entity and the resulting flag gates `path_type` only. The axis that was actually detected is the one left ungated.
survived.user_impact: On a Eufy model outside the x10/x8 families (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:226, `"supports_path_control": model_family in {"x10", "x8"}`) with no cleaning-intensity entity, the framework has determined the device has no intensity axis, suppresses path_type from the payload — and still sends `clean_intensity: "Quick"` (or "Deep") in every room dict of the room_clean command. survived.title: A user-authored leading or trailing charge/wait step is silently deleted at dispatch while the card still shows it and stamps has_charge_steps
survived.mechanism:
`while phases and phases[0].get("phase_type") in _BREAKS: phases.pop(0)` / `while phases and phases[-1].get("phase_type") in _BREAKS: phases.pop()` (run_plan.py:884-887). The stated rationale — "A break with no clean to bracket is pointless" (880-882) — is false for a LEADING break: `[charge_wait(95), room_group(...)]` has a clean immediately after it, and "charge to 95%, then clean" is a coherent plan; the same holds for a trailing "top up to 100% after the run".

These are the same defect reported by different agents: {A2-PP-CAP-1, A3-PP-CRUD-1} inert-catalog on apply_room_profile; {A1-PP-RES-2, A3-PP-CRUD-2, A6-PP-EST-DSP-1} the candidate/room water precedence asymmetry and its display consequence; {A1-PP-RES-5, A2-PP-CAP-4} the get_available_profile_names filter; {A1-PP-RES-8, A2-PP-CAP-7} the falsy-`or` catalog merge (RES-8 is the fuller write-up — it adds the line-289 KeyError); {A3-PP-CRUD-8, A4-PP-RP-5} the second-resolution id generator; {A1-PP-RES-4, A6-PP-EST-H2O-1} granite/concrete missing from the water tables; {A1-PP-RES-7, A3-PP-CRUD-3} orphaned profile references. Roughly 40 distinct defects, not 49.

HIGHEST-VALUE NEW GROUND (beyond the seven known soft spots): A6-PP-EST-BLK-1 (the mid-job reachability walk is queue-scoped where its start-plan sibling is map-scoped — a genuinely new, provable divergence that can cancel a live run), A4-PP-RP-2 (overwrite destroys a saved step sequence while save preserves it, reachable from the editor's only Save button because the card gates on has_charge_steps instead of has_stops), A4-PP-RP-1 (stepped profiles silently discard their saved per-room settings — the comment at manager.py:976-981 asserts a design the code does not implement), A4-PP-RP-3 (start_run_profile persists the room mutation before the start is allowed and never reverts), and A5-PP-RP-3 (Roborock IndexError out of get_start_status, with the guard written for that exact state sequenced after the throw).

CAVEATS FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: A6-PP-EST-BLK-1's mechanism is proven but its destructive arms are opt-in (path_block_action defaults to event_only), hence HIGH not CRITICAL — the default outcome is a false blocked-rooms event. A6-PP-EST-DSP-2's dead-logic claim is airtight but the symptom only survives on the build_room_payload/get_payload_state path, not the run-plan path where _match_profile_from_fields re-derives the name first. A3-PP-CRUD-5's reachability requires clean_intensity='Narrow' with a stale path_type='narrow', which is constructible but unlikely. Findings tagged future_brand_only (RES-8, CAP-7, CRUD-6, RP-7, RP-8/A5, H2O-2) are all genuinely unreachable on shipped hardware — they earn their severity as structural seams under rule 4, not as bugs to fix urgently.

Verified 45 findings by reading the three subsystem files in full plus the adjacent code every finding depended on (queue/queue_engine.py, queue/dispatch_engines.py, core/manager.py room/queue/start paths, rooms/room_crud.py, rooms/room_manager.py, rooms/room_defaults.py, rooms/access_graph.py, maps/map_manager.py, models/models.py, step_types.py, jobs/job_monitor.py, jobs/active_job.py, listeners/path_blockers.py, services/run_profiles.py, button.py, sensor/profile.py, learning/estimator.py, both adapters, and the card's run-profile / steps-order / room-profile state and bindings). Where a claim was executable I ran the real functions rather than reasoning about them.

VERDICT SUMMARY: 42 real, 3 false.

The three rejections:
- A1-PP-RES-1 (CRITICAL): the resolver bug is real but is rescued at BOTH dispatch payload builders. The finder enumerated callers of the private `_protected_room_config` and missed the public delegator `protected_room_config` at core/manager.py:2499 (build_room_payload) and planning/run_plan.py:1309 (start plan). Every room reaching queue_engine is already carpet/mop-protected; get_effective_room_details protects too, so neither the wire nor the label is wrong. The genuine bypass of that protection is A4-PP-RP-6 (the per-group step overlay), which I confirmed.
- A4-PP-RP-8 (LOW): built on "a Roborock room has no clean_intensity key". It always has one — models/models.py:208 `clean_intensity: str = ""` plus RoomConfig(...).as_dict() at both room writers — so the Eufy `.get(..., "Quick")` defaults it names are unreachable dead code, not injections. Its own sibling A2-PP-CAP-2 states the correct fact.
- A2-PP-CAP-5 (MEDIUM): the absent-key half is unreachable (the gate is only ever called on resolve output, which materialises all keys) and the empty-value half is the codebase's own declared "nobody said" convention producing no wrong output on either brand. No triggering case.

DUPLICATES — these are ONE finding each, counted twice by different agents; please de-duplicate before the fix ledger: {A1-PP-RES-2, A3-PP-CRUD-2}; {A2-PP-CAP-1, A3-PP-CRUD-1}; {A1-PP-RES-5, A2-PP-CAP-4}; {A1-PP-RES-8, A2-PP-CAP-7}; {A3-PP-CRUD-8, A4-PP-RP-5}; and A1-PP-RES-4 / A6-PP-EST-H2O-1 share one root (granite/concrete missing from the water tables) with two distinct consequences.

SEVERITY CORRECTIONS (13): downgraded A1-PP-RES-3 (legacy-room-only reachability), A2-PP-CAP-3 (contract violation, no demonstrated wrong device behaviour), A4-PP-RP-5, A5-PP-RP-2 (the always-reachable half is the known DQ-Q-3 lead), A5-PP-RP-4 (dead code; its impact is already counted in RP-5), A5-PP-RP-6, A5-PP-RP-7, A6-PP-EST-H2O-2, A6-PP-EST-GUESS-1, A6-PP-EST-DSP-1, A6-PP-EST-DSP-2, and A6-PP-EST-BLK-1 (CRITICAL->HIGH: the shipped default path_block_action is event_only, so the default outcome is a false block event; the cancel/pause outcomes need an explicit non-default option). Raised A2-PP-CAP-7 to MEDIUM only for consistency with its duplicate A1-PP-RES-8 under methodology rule 4.

HIGHEST-CONFIDENCE, ACT-FIRST SET (all reproduced against real code, all reachable on shipped hardware):
1. A4-PP-RP-2 (CRITICAL, data destruction) — overwrite_run_profile:1086 writes `"steps": []` and the card opens a wait-only/zone-only/multi-group profile's editor COLLAPSED because src/state/run-profiles.js:258 gates stepsExpanded on has_charge_steps instead of has_stops. Renaming a profile silently deletes its sequence.
2. A1-PP-RES-2 / A3-PP-CRUD-2 (HIGH) — executed the full pipeline over 32 profile x floor combinations: every built-in mop profile on hardwood/laminate/marble/granite/concrete lands on "custom", and vacuum_mop_deep on low-pile carpet mis-attributes to vacuum_deep. Existing tests PM-10/PM-10b pass because they build the room from a floor-less resolve rather than from apply_room_profile.
3. A6-PP-EST-BLK-1 (HIGH) — the mid-job reachability walk is queue-scoped while the start-plan walk is map-scoped; any subset run whose access parent is not queued is reported blocked on the next blocker-entity transition, in either direction.
4. A5-PP-RP-3 (HIGH, Roborock) — _build_steps_phases can return [] and `phases[0]` raises inside get_start_status BEFORE the all_selected_rooms_blocked guard written for that exact state.
5. A4-PP-RP-1 / A5-PP-RP-1 (HIGH) — get_queue_steps emits id-only room groups, so a saved stepped profile restores no settings; and no planner gate treats "more than one room_group" as stepped, so the canonical vacuum-then-mop profile is flattened to one pass while the card shows it sequenced.

A cross-cutting note the campaign may want: five separate findings (RES-2, CRUD-2, CAP-2, CRUD-4, EST-DSP-1) all trace to _match_profile_from_fields / get_effective_room_details resolving a candidate with neither the room's full field set nor the brand's catalog. One helper that resolves BOTH sides identically — same catalog, same key set — closes all five at a single seam.
